documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning
documents.title: Guidance on the Use of AI in Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: Provost-office guidance for instructors. It leaves AI permissions to each instructor and asks for syllabus statements covering assessed and non-assessed work, detection and consequences. It also covers AI in grading, distrust of detectors, copyright uploads and FERPA.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Authorization is determined at the course level by the instructor' and that instructors 'should determine and inform students when the use of AI is authorized or unauthorized'; it sets no university-wide permission or ban, so it delegates.

units.why: The page opens by saying 'We encourage students and faculty together to innovate learning through AI', a welcoming stance toward AI use by everyone, so it is a default-stance statement (P02), general phase, encourage.
units.anchor: We encourage students and faculty together to innovate learning through AI

units.why: This states the purpose and scope of the page ('to provide reasonably thorough, but also accessible and brief, guidance to support the AI approaches and practices of instructors'), an institution-level framing preamble, so P56, informs.
units.anchor: provide reasonably thorough, but also accessible and brief, guidance to support the AI approaches and

units.why: 'will be updated each semester and is expected to evolve' says the guidance is provisional and revised on a cycle, which is P54.
units.anchor: The guidance for instructors will be updated each semester and is expected to evolve

units.why: The office promises 'equivalent guidance specifically for students' based on input, a commitment to extend the guidance with feedback, so nearest type is P54 although it adds a student-facing guidance plan.
units.anchor: based on your input, we will develop equivalent guidance specifically for students
units.fit_note: Also says student-facing guidance will be written; P54 only covers revisiting and feedback.

units.why: Points instructors to the Teaching@Purdue module as resources for faculty learning about AI (P63).
units.anchor: Additional resources for Purdue instructors can be found in the

units.why: The monthly 'AI Teaching & Learning Digest' with news, research and faculty stories is ongoing faculty support (P63).
units.anchor: sign up for the AI Teaching & Learning Digest letter

units.why: Lists 'existing university policies and regulations that are relevant to the use of AI' (IP, copyright, acceptable use, conduct); AI use must be read within those, so P77.
units.anchor: existing university policies and regulations that are relevant to the use of AI in Purdue

units.why: 'Instructors should strive for maximum transparency and clarity in their communications to students about the use of AI' tells instructors to communicate AI expectations; closest to P09, though it states a general communication standard rather than a syllabus requirement.
units.anchor: Instructors should strive for maximum transparency and clarity in their communications to students about the
units.fit_note: Asks for maximum transparency and clarity generally, not specifically a syllabus statement.

units.why: Quotes the student conduct regulation that unauthorized 'materials, information, study aids, notes, or any other device' will not be tolerated; this makes use of anything the instructor has not approved a violation, so it is the misconduct classification (P36).
units.anchor: Using or attempting to use unauthorized materials, information, study aids, notes, or any other device
units.fit_note: Regulation is not AI-specific; AI is treated as an unauthorized aid by implication.

units.why: 'Unauthorized materials may include anything which or anyone who gives a student assistance that has not been approved by the instructor in advance' sets a default of not allowed unless approved in advance, i.e. a fallback rule (P06).
units.anchor: anything which or anyone who gives a student assistance that has not been approved by
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific and not about syllabus silence; it defines unauthorized assistance as anything not approved in advance.

units.why: 'the instructor, therefore, should determine and inform students when the use of AI is authorized or unauthorized' puts the decision with each instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: The instructor, therefore, should determine and inform students when the use of AI is authorized

units.why: 'Authorization is determined at the course level by the instructor' repeats who decides but adds the level (course), so it is coded as P04, not P11, because it does not say that permissions do not carry over.
units.anchor: Authorization is determined at the course level by the instructor.

units.why: Instructors 'should include specific guidance on' allowable AI use, an instruction to state AI expectations on the syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: On the course syllabus, instructors should include specific guidance on

units.why: 'Allowable use of AI tools by students for assessed work in the course' with the example of homework: syllabus must say what is allowed on graded work, P09.
units.anchor: Allowable use of AI tools by students for assessed work in the course.

units.why: 'Appropriate use of AI tools by students during the learning process for non-assessed work' (example: summarizing a reading) asks the syllabus to cover non-graded use separately from graded use, still P09.
units.anchor: Appropriate use of AI tools by students during the learning process for non-assessed work of
units.fit_note: Also separates assessed from non-assessed work, implying different rules for each.

units.why: The syllabus should explain 'The ways in which the instructional team may attempt to detect the use of AI'; this is a detection-disclosure duty, closest to P40 but what is required is telling students, so a fit note is added.
units.anchor: The ways in which the instructional team may attempt to detect the use of AI
units.fit_note: Requires telling students how detection may happen, not mandating a method.

units.why: The syllabus should state 'The potential consequences faced by students who violate the AI use policies', i.e. consequences stated in advance (P37), though no specific penalty is named here.
units.anchor: The potential consequences faced by students who violate the AI use policies in the course.
units.fit_note: Requires stating consequences but gives no specific penalties.

units.why: 'The instructor of record is responsible and accountable for all grades on all assessments' places grading responsibility on a human, in keeping with P46 (humans assign grades), though it does not mention AI directly.
units.anchor: The instructor of record is responsible and accountable for all grades on all assessments in
units.fit_note: General principle of grade accountability; AI is implied by the section context.

units.why: 'All assigned grades must be explainable and defendable based upon evidence submitted by the student' constrains how any grading, including AI-assisted, is done; fits P46 loosely.
units.anchor: All assigned grades must be explainable and defendable based upon evidence submitted by the student
units.fit_note: Requires explainable grades but does not itself say a human must assign them.

units.why: Delegating grading to TAs with the instructor keeping 'responsibility for oversight' is about instructional-team roles, not AI use per se and fits no type well, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Some grading responsibilities may be delegated by the instructor of record to other members of
units.uncovered_note: Instructors may delegate grading to TAs but keep oversight and accountability.

units.why: When AI tools are used in grading, instructors 'should create and apply a process' so grades are 'explainable and defendable'; this governs instructors' own AI use in grading, closest to P59, with the human-in-the-loop part coded separately.
units.anchor: Create and apply a process by which any AI-based tools used for grading student work
units.fit_note: Permits AI-based grading tools by implication but conditions them on an explainability process.

units.why: 'Ensure that a human remains in the loop to the maximum extent possible' keeps people responsible for grading with AI, matching P46 (humans, not AI, assign grades), softened by 'to the maximum extent possible'.
units.anchor: Ensure that a human remains in the loop to the maximum extent possible.
units.fit_note: Human in the loop 'to the maximum extent possible' is weaker than a rule that humans assign grades.

units.why: Asks for 'a quality assurance procedure to ensure grading automation features ... work accurately', a rule on how instructors use automated grading tools, so P59 (instructor AI use for teaching work).
units.anchor: Integrate a quality assurance procedure to ensure grading automation features

units.why: 'Avoid blackbox grading methods/tools that cannot be validated or explained' limits which AI grading tools instructors may use, P59.
units.anchor: methods/tools that cannot be validated or explained

units.why: 'Consider the appropriateness of using AI detection tools' asks instructors to weigh detectors before using them, pointing to the AI-detection section; nearest P39 (do not rely on detectors) but it is only a prompt to consider.
units.anchor: Consider the appropriateness of using AI detection tools
units.fit_note: Only asks instructors to consider whether detectors are appropriate; does not say not to use them.

units.why: 'Current AI detection tools have very high false-positive rates, rendering them almost useless in practice' is the core P39 statement that detectors are unreliable.
units.anchor: Current AI detection tools have very high false-positive rates

units.why: Instructors 'should treat any results generated via AI detection tools, including those in TurnItIn, with extreme distrust', a direct instruction not to rely on detector output, P39.
units.anchor: treat any results generated via AI detection tools, including those in TurnItIn, with extreme distrust

units.why: Instructors should 'carefully review suspected cases with due diligence and according to a procedure clearly explained to students', which sets a standard of care in finding misuse (P69) and a requirement to explain the procedure in advance.
units.anchor: carefully review suspected cases with due diligence and according to a procedure clearly explained to
units.fit_note: Due diligence plus a procedure explained on the syllabus; no explicit evidence standard.

units.why: Instructors should 'clearly describe the specific ways in which they will (or will not) attempt to detect the unauthorized use of AI', a syllabus disclosure duty about detection; coded P40 as the home for detection practice with a fit note.
units.anchor: Clearly describe the specific ways in which they will (or will not) attempt to detect
units.fit_note: Duty to describe detection (or its absence), not a mandate to detect.

units.why: The syllabus should give 'the procedures they will follow if an unauthorized use of AI is suspected', a duty to publish the misuse process in advance; no type is about publishing the process, so P36 is the nearest with a fit note.
units.anchor: The procedures they will follow if an unauthorized use of AI is suspected.
units.fit_note: Requires stating the suspicion procedure on the syllabus; not itself the classification as misconduct.

units.why: 'a positive result from one of these tools is not the sole determining factor of an academic integrity violation' sets what evidence suffices, so P69.
units.anchor: a positive result from one of these tools is not the sole determining factor of

units.why: Syllabus should state 'potential consequences ... including any impacts on grades and possible referral to the Office of Student Rights and Responsibilities', which names the grade impact and the escalation route; P37 with fit note (no concrete penalty).
units.anchor: including any impacts on grades and possible referral to the Office of Student Rights and
units.fit_note: Names grade impact and referral to the integrity office but no specific penalty.

units.why: Notes that some tools 'encourage users to upload copyrighted material as training data'; this explains the copyright risk of AI tools (P52), informs.
units.anchor: Some AI based tools encourage users to upload copyrighted material as training data

units.why: Instructors should 'make clear to students that sharing of copyrighted material with third-party AI tools is prohibited', an upload ban (P49).
units.anchor: sharing of copyrighted material with third-party AI tools is prohibited

units.why: Instructor-generated materials 'should never be uploaded to any third-party site (whether AI oriented or not)' is a ban on uploading course notes, slides and assessments, P49.
units.anchor: those instructor-generated materials should never be uploaded to any third-party site (whether AI oriented or

units.why: Reminding students that instructors 'do own copyright to their expression, explanation, and presentation' of facts in notes, slides and assessments states ownership of course materials, P52.
units.anchor: they do own copyright to their expression, explanation, and presentation of those facts and ideas

units.why: Some tools 'use user-supplied data to further train their models'; informs about privacy risk, P50.
units.anchor: use user-supplied data to further train their models

units.why: 'instructors must--as always--comply with FERPA requirements for student information and privacy' is a binding duty on instructors using AI tools, P50.
units.anchor: instructors must-as always-comply with FERPA requirements for student information and privacy

units.why: Instructors should 'clearly communicate with students how their data or interactions with AI tools may be used or shared before an instructor puts any of the student's work into an AI tool, including AI detectors', which is disclosure of the instructor's own AI use to students (P47).
units.anchor: before an instructor puts any of the student's work into an AI tool, including AI

units.why: Instructors should 'commit to never sharing personally identifiable information about students with any third-party AI tool', a limit on instructor AI use; P47 covers committing to limits, but the main point is data protection (P50), which I chose.
units.anchor: Commit to never sharing personally identifiable information about students with any third-party AI tool

units.why: Instructors should 'obtain students' consent to share data on their interactions with AI when appropriate', e.g. in research, a consent duty tied to data protection (P50).
units.anchor: they will obtain students' consent to share data on their interactions with AI when appropriate
units.fit_note: Consent for sharing interaction data, including for research; P50 is mostly about protecting data.

units.why: The university 'is working toward expanding our technology-based teaching and learning environments' where AI tools can be built and used with protected content, a plan for sanctioned environments (P17), not yet available.
units.anchor: The university is working toward expanding our technology-based teaching and learning environments
units.fit_note: Describes future planned environments, not an existing sanctioned tool.

units.why: 'Please plan to bring your ideas and teaching technology environment needs to the Spring 2024 town hall' invites feedback on needs, P54.
units.anchor: bring your ideas and teaching technology environment needs to the Spring 2024 town hall

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Use (VII.A.5)
documents.summary: An IT policy issued November 2025 on GenAI and LLM use across the university. It authorizes approved tools, restricts sensitive data, bars AI as the sole basis for personnel, award or disciplinary decisions, and requires incident reporting and training. Classroom use is deferred to the provost guidelines.
documents.stance_why: Policy VII.A.5 says 'The responsible use of approved AI tools and technologies is authorized subject to the following requirements', which allows AI with conditions on data, approved tools and review; classroom decisions are left to 'Provost guidelines'.

units.why: Defines 'Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLM), collectively referred to as AI in this policy', fixing the scope of the term, P61.
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLM), collectively referred to as AI in

units.why: 'Responsible use ... is essential to the University's ongoing mission' states the purpose and principle of the policy, P56.
units.anchor: is essential to the University's ongoing mission

units.why: 'AI tools and the university data used with them are IT Resources and Information Assets ... subject to the Acceptable Use policy' places AI under existing IT policy, P77.
units.anchor: AI tools and the university data used with them are IT Resources and Information Assets

units.why: 'usage must not violate any local, state or federal law or regulation or any university policy' requires legal and policy compliance, P77.
units.anchor: usage must not violate any local, state or federal law or regulation or any university

units.why: 'The responsible use of approved AI tools and technologies is authorized subject to the following requirements' allows AI use with conditions, a permit-by-default for approved tools (P02), though it is limited to approved tools.
units.anchor: The responsible use of approved AI tools and technologies is authorized subject to the following
units.fit_note: Permission is conditional and limited to approved AI tools.

units.why: 'Sensitive and Restricted Data ... must not be entered into AI tools without prior approval' bans entering protected data, P50.
units.anchor: Sensitive and Restricted Data, as defined in the Acceptable Use policy, must not be entered

units.why: Approval requires that the tool be 'approved for Sensitive and/or Restricted Data use ... per the approved AI tools list' and the use case approved by the Data Ethics Committee, i.e. use of vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: The tool is approved for Sensitive and/or Restricted Data use as applicable per the approved
units.fit_note: Also requires committee approval of the use case.

units.why: 'AI tool development and implementation processes must follow the Data Ethics Committee's guidance' governs building AI tools for university use, an operational rule, P76.
units.anchor: AI tool development and implementation processes must follow the Data Ethics Committee's guidance.

units.why: 'AI may be used to inform decision makers, but it must not be the sole factor used in making personnel, award or disciplinary decisions' is the human-decides rule, P73.
units.anchor: it must not be the sole factor used in making personnel, award or disciplinary decisions

units.why: 'Unit heads are responsible for determining the extent to which AI may be used to inform decision-makers in their respective areas' delegates the extent of use to units, P04 (who decides), although for administrative decisions rather than assignments.
units.anchor: Unit heads are responsible for determining the extent to which AI may be used
units.fit_note: Delegation is to unit heads for decision-making support, not to instructors for coursework.

units.why: 'Provost guidelines provide guidance for academic and classroom usage' hands classroom rules to a separate document (the CTL guidance), so this is a scope and framework pointer, P56.
units.anchor: Provost guidelines provide guidance for academic and classroom usage.
units.fit_note: Scope statement that leaves classroom rules to a separate document.

units.why: Users must 'always review and ensure AI output is accurate, appropriately cited, does not contain Restricted Data ... and minimizes bias or misinformation' before sharing; main thrust is verifying output (P31), also covering citation and data.
units.anchor: always review and ensure AI output is accurate, appropriately cited
units.fit_note: Also requires appropriate citation, no Restricted Data and minimized bias; one compound sentence.

units.why: 'A New IT Solutions and Services Review is required for use of any AI tools ... not already on the approved AI tools list' requires vetting before use, P50.
units.anchor: A New IT Solutions and Services Review is required for use of any AI tools

units.why: 'the user(s) must immediately report the incident' when non-public data is uploaded to an unapproved AI tool is a duty to report data exposure, P71.
units.anchor: the user(s) must immediately report the incident

units.why: 'Purdue University supports responsible, measured experimentation with and use of new technologies' gives the rationale for allowing AI, P56.
units.anchor: Purdue University supports responsible, measured experimentation with and use of new technologies

units.why: Warns that information entered into AI tools without an agreement 'may become the property of the tool provider and be used in training', a data and IP risk, P50.
units.anchor: may become the property of the tool provider and be used in training its services

units.why: 'Responsible use of AI is essential to maintaining academic integrity, data security and institutional standards' states why the policy exists, P56.
units.anchor: Responsible use of AI is essential to maintaining academic integrity, data security and institutional standards.

units.why: The policy applies to 'All Purdue persons, departments, units, contractors, consultants and campuses using AI' and has 'no exclusions', which sets scope, P56.
units.anchor: All Purdue persons, departments, units, contractors, consultants and campuses using AI.

units.why: Faculty, staff, students and others must 'use AI in compliance with this policy', a general compliance duty, P77.
units.anchor: Use AI in compliance with this policy.

units.why: Users must 'complete applicable training on appropriate use of AI as required by Purdue IT', a training mandate, P70.
units.anchor: Complete applicable training on appropriate use of AI as required by Purdue IT.

units.why: The CISO is told to 'oversee ongoing implementation of this policy', assigning ownership; no type covers role assignment for maintaining a policy, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Oversee ongoing implementation of this policy.
units.uncovered_note: Names the CISO as responsible for overseeing implementation of the AI use policy.

units.why: Purdue Systems Security must 'implement monitoring to identify and remediate policy violations', an institutional monitoring duty for IT misuse; no type fits since it is not coursework detection, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Implement monitoring to identify and remediate policy violations.
units.uncovered_note: IT security staff monitor to identify and remediate violations of the AI use policy.

units.why: Systems Security must 'process policy exceptions', an exception procedure for the AI policy that fits no listed type, UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Process policy exceptions.
units.uncovered_note: A process exists to grant exceptions to the AI use policy.

units.why: The Data Ethics Committee must 'ensure appropriate legal agreements are in place with third-party AI tools', a review of vendor agreements, P65.
units.anchor: Ensure appropriate legal agreements are in place with third-party AI tools

units.why: Committee must 'ensure any approved AI tool put into use follows Purdue's AI Guiding Principles', pointing to an institutional principles framework, P56.
units.anchor: Ensure any approved AI tool put into use follows Purdue's AI Guiding Principles.
units.fit_note: Refers to separate AI Guiding Principles whose content is not in this text.

units.why: Committee will 'provide recommendations on policy changes regarding the use of AI', a mechanism for revising the policy, P54.
units.anchor: Provide recommendations on policy changes regarding the use of AI at Purdue.

units.why: Committee must 'consider potential reputational harm from the implementation of Purdue-facing AI tools', an operational review concern about public-facing AI, P76.
units.anchor: Consider potential reputational harm from the implementation of Purdue-facing AI tools.

units.why: Committee will 'review and approve enterprise-level training modules on appropriate use of AI', training provided to the community, P70.
units.anchor: Review and approve enterprise-level training modules on appropriate use of AI.

units.why: The history says the policy was 'reviewed, no changes' in 2026, evidence of a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: Policy reviewed, no changes.

notes: Only the two included university-layer documents were coded; school/computing none-found, course deferred. VII.A.5 is an IT/data policy and says little about coursework. The CTL page mentions a Spring 2024 town hall, so parts of it may predate its August 2025 modification.
